task/easy: Turning an image into noise is easy: one blend, and no learning needed.
task/hard: The other way is hard. Handed only the noisy picture, which part of it is static?
task/job: That is what a diffusion model's network learns: to find the noise in a noised image. Taking noise out is called denoising.
task/sees: It is shown only the noised image, x t, and the step t, which says how much noise to look for: never x zero or epsilon alone.
task/asks: Out comes its guess of the noise, the same shape as the image, written epsilon hat: a hat marks an estimate.
task/learn: To do that, it must learn what images look like: whatever does not look like part of one is noise.
loss/loss: Training needs one number for how wrong a guess is: the loss, the f that gradient descent pushes down.
loss/free: Here the right answer is known, since the noise was drawn on purpose: the target is epsilon itself.
loss/three: Take three pixels: the noise that went in, and the guess, side by side.
loss/miss: At the first pixel, the noise was zero point five and the guess zero point three: a miss of zero point two.
loss/others: The second misses by minus zero point four, and the third by zero point five.
loss/cancel: Averaging the misses as they are lets them cancel: a miss up and a miss down add to nothing.
loss/square: So square each one. A square is never negative, and a miss twice as big costs four times as much.
loss/squares: Zero point two squared is zero point zero four. The other two give zero point one six and zero point two five.
loss/mean: Together, zero point four five. Over three pixels, that is zero point one five: the loss.
loss/name: The name reads it backwards: each error, squared, then their mean. The mean squared error.
loss/ho: In 2020, Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain and Pieter Abbeel trained this way. Asking for the clean image directly had made worse images.
loss/simple: Their theory gave each step's error its own weight. They dropped the weights, kept this plain squared error, called L simple, and got better images.
batch/pick: One step of training takes a random minibatch of B clean images.
batch/t: Each gets its own random step t and fresh noise, so one batch mixes every task: a light dusting here, almost pure static there.
batch/guess: The network guesses the noise in every one of them.
batch/step: The loss averages the squared misses over every pixel of every image, and a gradient step pushes it down.
image/also: A guess of the noise is also a guess of the image: peel the guessed noise away from x t, and the image is what is left.
image/undo: The noise went in scaled by the root of one minus alpha bar, so take the guess away scaled the same. Then divide by the root of alpha bar, which shrank the image.
image/hat: The result is written x zero hat: an estimate of the clean image.
image/worse: The better the noise guess, the cleaner the estimate. A poor guess leaves static behind.
image/pixel: Follow one pixel: zero point five, at an alpha bar of zero point six four, with a noise guess of minus a half.
image/scaled: Scaled by zero point six, the guess is minus zero point three.
image/sub: Taking away minus zero point three adds it: zero point five plus zero point three is zero point eight.
image/div: Divide by zero point eight, the root of zero point six four: the estimate of the clean pixel is one.
